subject: EXCEPTION-OBJECT
notes: kb/Work PB922 (wave 42) - RULE (cite.py --check 8.4.3.6.3 'EXCEPTION-OBJECT is implicitly described as class object and category object reference, as an external data item, and as a universal object reference'): OK, SR2. The STANDARD declares this name and no data description entry does, so a resolver that does not know it answers 'is not defined' about a name that is defined - which is what every sending reference got. DataBinder.ExceptionObjectRegister now carries SR2's implicit description (PicInfo.ObjectReferenceItem(ObjectRefDescriptor.Universal)) and ReferenceResolver resolves the bare word to an ExceptionObjectPlace over it, beside the CAPACITY and DEBUG-ITEM registers, so every class/category screen reads it like any other object-reference item and every caller inherits the answer. It is a VIEW, never storage: 8.4.3.6.4 GR2 gives the run unit ONE instance, which is the runtime's ExceptionState, and PlaceRenderer renders the read (fully qualified, because a reference to it needs neither the EC model nor a class and the conditional 'using' would otherwise leave the backend with CS0103 on generated C# the user cannot see). MEASURED at 2002 and 2023: IF EXCEPTION-OBJECT = NULL is legal source and true when no exception object is associated with the current exception (GR1); SET U TO EXCEPTION-OBJECT copies that reference; two references denote the same instance (GR2). SR2's 'as an external data item' is deliberately NOT carried as HasExternalClause - that flag drives the 13.18.22 EXTERNAL-store re-basing of a DECLARED record, and what the phrase asserts (one instance per run unit) is already realized by the single ExceptionState. ExceptionObjectPlace is registered in PlaceStorageFormSwitchDriftTests' storage-form roster, so a switch that meets it in a catch-all is a failing test.
